title: Panchavati
hook: a cold winter dawn by the river, and a brother says one sentence too many

segments.voice: Yesterday: Panchavati, part one. Jatayu promised to guard Sita, and Lakshmana built the hut by the Godavari. Did you make a corner of home better for someone? Today the week closes. Day five hundred sixty.

Time passes at Panchavati, and the season turns to hemanta, the cold season, early winter. One morning before sunrise, the three of them walk down to the Godavari to bathe. Lakshmana carries the water pot. And as they go, he talks, the way people do on cold walks. Mist over the fields. The sun weak and far away. Water so cold that, he says, even the elephants touch it with their trunks and pull back.
screen: `HEMANTA: THE COLD SEASON.` → `A WALK TO THE RIVER AT DAWN.` → `EVEN THE ELEPHANTS PULL BACK.`

segments.voice: Then Lakshmana's mind goes home. Right now, he says, Bharata is probably walking down to the Sarayu in this same cold, to bathe before dawn. He could be living in a palace. Instead he sleeps on the ground and keeps the vows of an ascetic, out of love for you. And then he adds the sentence. How could a mother like Kaikeyi have a son like Bharata? Rama stops him. Don't speak badly of our middle mother, he says. Speak only of Bharata. And then Rama says how much he misses him: Bharata's sweet, kind words, which Rama says come back to him like nectar. He longs to see him, and Shatrughna, and all of them. Rama, who lost a kingdom to Kaikeyi's wish, is the one who won't allow the bitterness. He doesn't argue that Kaikeyi was right. He just won't let the conversation turn sour. Now the week. Viradha, the giant who was a cursed musician. Sharabhanga, who waited to see Rama before going to heaven, and the bones that brought Rama's promise. Sita's question about weapons, and Rama's answer. Agastya, who digested a demon and gave Rama a god's bow. Jatayu's offer to guard Sita. And Panchavati: a hut by a river, a brother's handiwork, and now, a cold morning where blame is stopped before it settles in. This quiet is about to end.
screen: `BHARATA IN THE SAME COLD.` · `HOW COULD SHE HAVE SUCH A SON?` · `SPEAK ONLY OF BHARATA.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `BLAME STOPPED AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Sit and imagine the cool air of an early morning. Feel the breath coming in a little cool through the nose, and leaving warm. Now think of someone you've been tempted to complain about lately. Instead, bring to mind someone connected to them whom you love or admire. Let your attention stay with the one you admire. Breathe in cool, breathe out warm, and keep coming back to the good one. The bell holds the time.
Panchavati. A winter dawn by the Godavari, where Rama tells Lakshmana: don't speak badly of our middle mother. Speak of Bharata.
Your line: Panchavati. Today, when a conversation turns to blaming someone, steer it toward someone worth praising. Day five hundred sixty.

screen: `DAY 560 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK DEEPER INTO THE FOREST, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: SHURPANAKHA.`

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers cite Rama's refusal to let Lakshmana speak ill of Kaikeyi as an example of restraint in speech within a family.

fork.setup: you're Rama. your brother, on a cold walk, says something bitter about the stepmother who exiled you. what do you do?
options: stop him, and talk about Bharata instead.
fork.reveal: Rama says: don't speak badly of our middle mother. speak only of Bharata. then he says how much he misses him.

original.note: Sanskrit hemanta: the early-winter season, one of the traditional seasons of the Indian year.

trapdoor: what you thought: Panchavati is where nothing much happens.
what it means: in the quiet, Rama refuses to let blame settle on Kaikeyi.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 16 is a famous season poem that turns into a lesson on speech: Rama silences blame and turns to praise.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 16 (the winter morning; Lakshmana on Bharata and Kaikeyi; Rama's reply)
